subject: Follow-up: continuous batching & concurrency assumptions for Stripetech PoC
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@stripetech.com>; Ben Lewis <ben.lewis@stripetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Stripetech PoC — traffic & pricing checkpoints

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can model a concrete PoC: 

1) Confirmed traffic profile (ballpark)
   - Expected production peak: 1,800 concurrent requests during US morning spike
   - Steady-state concurrent: ~250 requests
   - Average request length: 400 tokens (prompt + expected response)
   - Long-tail: 3% of requests > 2,000 tokens (batching behavior important)

2) Continuous batching expectation
   - You mentioned a preference for continuous batching (small batching windows to reduce latency) versus fixed windows. We'll assume 20–40ms continuous windows with adaptive packing unless you ask for manual windowing.

3) Target economics
   - You indicated a target overall unit basis of ~$750 per 1M tokens for the PoC (includes modest reserved capacity and some burst credit). Please confirm if that target is $/1M tokens invoiced to you.

4) Proof-of-concept scope and asks
   - Stripetech to provide 24–72h sample traffic CSV (timestamps, avg token length, request type flag). Attachment: stripetech_traffic_sample.csv (placeholder)
   - We will run a short simulation using continuous batching + KV prefix caching to estimate average per-token unit cost and tail latency.
   - Next call: align on SLA acceptance criteria and a pricing anchor to use for mutual action plan. I attached a draft MAP.

Next steps: Maya to confirm sample file + whether the $750/1M target is firm for the PoC. I’ll loop in engineering (Marissa) for any tuning we need to simulate concurrency windows.

Best,
Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Rao <maya@stripetech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Stripetech PoC — traffic & pricing checkpoints

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The $750/1M is our internal target to keep the PoC viable for leadership review, but procurement may push for a slightly lower anchor (~$650/1M) if the SLA commitments are strict. For modeling, please run both $650 and $750 scenarios.
- Concurrent numbers: the 1,800 concurrency is an upper bound seen during week-long promotional emails; typical marketing days are closer to 1,200 peak. We can include both spikes in the sample CSV.
- Token breakdown: our payloads are often prompt-heavy (system + user history), so please assume 60% of tokens come from prompt and 40% from generated tokens. We use streaming for real-time UI.

I’ve uploaded a short 48h sample extract to our shared Drive (link in your MAP). attaching the sample to this thread as well. Procurement will be cc’ed on the next email.

Maya
Maya Rao
Head of Integrations, StripeTech
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@stripetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com; procurement@stripetech.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Stripetech PoC — traffic & pricing checkpoints

Thanks Maya — got the sample and the Drive link, I pulled the 48h extract. Quick notes after a first pass and a few asks so we can size the PoC accurately: 

- Pricing scenarios: will model both $650 and $750 per 1M tokens. For each scenario we’ll show: avg cost/token, expected monthly bill at 100M / 500M / 1B token volumes, and expected reserve commitment that unlocks the anchor price.
- Batching/concurrency modeling assumptions:
   * Continuous batching window: 30ms nominal (adaptive).
   * Effective batch sizes from sample: median batch ~6 requests, 95th percentile batch ~24 requests.
   * Latency SLO target for PoC: p95 < 300ms for non-streamed responses; streamed responses measured by first-byte latency p50 < 120ms.
   * KV/prefix caching: assume 20% hit-rate from repeated system prompt prefixes (you mentioned common templates).

- Material impact levers we’ll surface: batching window, quantization profile (we’ll show INT8 vs FP16 delta), and reserved capacity vs on-demand mix.

Attachments: I added the mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_v1.docx) with proposed milestones.

Action items:
- Maya: confirm whether the 1,200 or 1,800 peak should be used for baseline simulation (we'll present both).
- Procurement: flag any hard constraints on data residency/SLA to include in the PoC scope.
- Marissa/Aditya: can you run the traffic simulation using the attached CSV and the continuous batching profile above and share a short table of projected $/1M and p95 latency for 100M/500M/1B token scenarios by EOD Wed?

Thanks — I’ll consolidate the numbers into a brief deck for the Friday call.

Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Stripetech PoC — traffic & pricing checkpoints

Looping back with the simulation status and preliminary numbers (first-pass): 

- Simulation assumptions used: continuous batching 30ms, median req length 400 tokens, peak concurrency 1,200 (baseline) / 1,800 (spike), 20% KV cache hit-rate, mixed quantization (INT8 for weight-heavy models).

Prelim results (rounded):
- 100M tokens/month: $710 / 1M tokens (avg) — p95 latency 260ms
- 500M tokens/month: $690 / 1M tokens (avg) — p95 latency 280ms
- 1B tokens/month: $670 / 1M tokens (avg) — p95 latency 320ms (higher tail during sustained spikes)

Notes: continuous batching materially reduces unit cost versus no-batching baseline (~18% savings). If we allow slightly larger adaptive windows (50–80ms) we can push the $/1M down by another 6–8% at the expense of p95 latency increasing ~30–50ms.

Attached: short CSV with the three scenario summaries (we'll add to the Drive). Next steps: I’ll prepare a two-slide summary for the Friday call showing the $650 and $750 anchors and the tradeoffs for latency vs cost under continuous batching.

Marissa
Product — Performance & Ops, Redwood Inference
